newsitem.title: USA: TWA pilots seek new contract talks.
newsitem.headline: TWA pilots seek new contract talks.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc's pilots are seeking to amend their current contract to get higher pay and scheduling changes, a statement from the pilots' union said.

"The pilots of TWA are seeking substantial improvements in scheduling and pay rates comparable to our counterparts at other major airlines," Don Jacobs, chairman of TWA's branch of the Air Line Pilots Association, said in a statement.
TWA spokesman John McDonald said contract talks with the pilots and the flight attendants will begin soon.
All of the carrier's labor contracts are set to expire August 31, 1997, McDonald said. The company is currently negotiating with the machinists union.
"We'll negotiate their contract, not through the press, but with them (the union)," McDonald said.
The union said that it understands that TWA is emerging from a year loss of $284.8 million, or $7.27 a share, on revenues of $3.55 billion.
However, the union said TWA's competitors "have been able to operate profitably with higher pilot pay rates and more efficient scheduling."

Marc Spiegel, the chairman of the union's negotiating committee, said a 767-300 captain at TWA with 15 years experience is paid $107.05 per flight hour, compared with an industry wide average of $174.18 per flight hour for a captain of the same size plane with 12 years experience.
Seniority lists for pilots do not transfer airline to airline, so TWA's pilots would not receive comparable pay if they changed airlines, Spiegel said.

As of November 1, 1996, the average first officer on a 727 with six years experience would be paid $91.44/flight hour, compared with $51.85 a flight hour for TWA's pilots, Spiegel said. Spiegel said some carriers have negotiated higher wages for their pilots since November 1.
TWA's McDonald said, "The highest paid pilots in the country at American said they were underpaid too."
